name: Wu Bong Sa
aka: Kwan Um School of Zen - Main Temple in Europe
tradition: Korean Zen (Kwan Um School of Zen)
technique: Zen sitting meditation, chanting and bowing practice, walking meditation (kinhin), formal Oryoki meals, koan interviews, and work practice (samu)
teacherAccess: Daily practice alongside resident teachers and the guiding teacher; individual interviews (mondo) with a Zen teacher during retreats and by arrangement.
retreatOptions: Weekend to roughly two-week Yong Maeng Jong Jin silent retreats; a 3-4 week summer Kyol Che and a 90-day winter Kyol Che intensive retreat each year; also flexible guest and resident stays of any length.
about: Wu Bong Sa is the main European temple of the Kwan Um School of Zen, founded by Zen Master Seung Sahn, occupying a house and garden in the Falenica district on Warsaw's southern edge. The Polish sangha has practiced here since 1982, making it one of the longest-running Zen communities in the country, and the temple hosts the school's flagship European retreats: a 90-day Kyol Che each winter and a 3-4 week Kyol Che each summer, alongside shorter Yong Maeng Jong Jin retreats that run from a weekend up to about two weeks. Days follow a traditional Korean Zen temple schedule of pre-dawn bows, chanting, multiple rounds of sitting and walking meditation, formal Oryoki meals, and work practice, with the option for retreatants to meet individually with a teacher. The temple is entirely vegetarian and alcohol- and smoking-free, and also takes short- and long-term guests and residents outside of scheduled retreats.
schedule: Daily morning (5:45am, Mon-Sat) and evening (Mon-Fri) practice plus occasional Sunday public sittings, with scheduled multi-day Yong Maeng Jong Jin retreats through the year and the annual winter (90-day) and summer (3-4 week) Kyol Che intensives.
cost: Daily practice is free/by donation; overnight guest and retreat accommodation is charged per night, with a discount for school members.

pricePerDay.notes: Guest accommodation: short-term guest 80 PLN/night (60 PLN for Kwan Um School members); long-term stay of over a week roughly 350 PLN/week (about 50 PLN/night), 250 PLN/week for members. Separate registration fees may apply for structured retreats such as Kyol Che.

foodNotes: The temple kitchen is entirely vegetarian and alcohol/smoking-free; retreat participants share communal meals (including formal Oryoki) as part of the daily schedule, while guests outside of retreats generally self-cater in the shared kitchen.
workNotes: Work practice (samu) is a scheduled part of each retreat day; guests staying at the temple outside of retreats are also asked to help with chores and zen work.
